title: Early warning: P-03
formula: risk × cost if it fails − cost of planned maintenance; maintenance pays when the risk is above planned ÷ unplanned
steps: Signal variability is 0.94 against 0.11 for its peers (as a share of the normal range). It explains 20.9 of the 21.7 points by which the risk score exceeds what age and load alone give.
Deviation from the twin is 0.14 against 0.05 for its peers (as a share of the normal range). It explains 0.8 of the 21.7 points by which the risk score exceeds what age and load alone give.

inputs.name: Risk score now
inputs.basis: The failure model's score for this asset, read against its synthetic history (not the chance of failing within a stated time).

inputs.name: Risk score from age and load alone
inputs.basis: The same score with the condition signals set to the median of the other assets of the same kind.

inputs.name: Cost if it fails
inputs.basis: Losses until the crew works (3,000 EGP/h) over the delay plus a late repair; cost model pump-failure proxy.

inputs.name: Deviation from the twin
inputs.basis: The median of the other assets of the same kind is 0.052.

inputs.name: Signal variability
inputs.basis: The median of the other assets of the same kind is 0.107.

inputs.name: planned_factor
inputs.basis: Planned work is budgeted at 60% of emergency crew-plus-parts cost. Verify against matched planned and emergency maintenance work orders.

inputs.name: customers_zone_cbd
inputs.basis: Planning service-account count scaled to the district demand in ZONE_BASE; residential accounts are households, institutional accounts are service connections, not people. Verify against the district occupancy and utility connection registers.

inputs.name: customer_hour_business
inputs.basis: Illustrative business account-hour budget for notification and utility customer support only; excludes customer economic harm covered by VoLL. Verify against the utility support cost ledger and outage notification work orders.

inputs.name: crew_callout
inputs.basis: Budget allowance for transport and emergency labour per dispatch. Verify against crew timesheets and the maintenance contractor rate card.

inputs.name: parts_pump
inputs.basis: Budget for a pump mechanical/electrical repair. Verify against the pump asset bill of materials and maintenance work orders.

inputs.name: delay_hours_pump_failure
inputs.basis: An idle failed pump requires slower mechanical restoration; this horizon is a planning scenario. Verify against fault-specific restoration logs and the response SLA.

inputs.name: response_hours
inputs.basis: One hour is a district dispatch-to-isolation planning allowance. Verify against dispatch logs and the emergency response SLA.

inputs.name: late_multiplier_pump_failure
inputs.basis: An idle failed pump requires slower mechanical restoration; the multiplier is a planning allowance, not an estimated growth law. Verify against matched early and deferred repair work orders.

notes: The warning opens when the risk score exceeds what age and load explain by 1.0 in log-odds, held for three readings in a row (about a minute), while the asset is still running and is not inside an open incident.

The score was checked against the history the model learned from: on 1,500 held-out assets its mean error against the true rate in that history is 4.6 points (Brier 0.154; 0.150 is the best any score can reach). That history has no time window and a failure is recorded for 50% of its assets, so the score is not the chance of failing within a stated time, and its level is high by construction.
The risk model is trained on a synthetic hazard: this shows the mechanism, not field accuracy. The expected saving treats the score as the chance of failing, which is an assumption.

In 24 test runs of a pump wearing out over 5 to 20 minutes and left alone, the warning came before the pump stopped in 24 of 24, a median 114 s before it (from 12 s to 574 s). At the moment of the warning the risk score ranged from 2% to 97%, so the level alone does not say how close the stop is. A wear of 3 minutes was too fast: warned in 2 of 6. No warning was raised in 24 simulated hours without a fault (0 false). The twin makes every wear end in a stop, so this shows that the warning comes in time, not that a real pump would fail.
